findings.title: `continue` inside `for x in xs` skips the index step: the loop never advances (same defect in the C-style form)
findings.why: The for-each form is desugared to `while __extc_i < __extc_s.len { var d = __extc_s[__extc_i] BODY __extc_i += 1 }` -- the increment is the last statement of the while body. A `continue` in the user body jumps to the condition, the index is never incremented, and the loop spins forever. `desugared->forDesugar = true` (parser.c:2465) does not help: the only reader is check_stmt.c:201 `forRetargetToIterator`, which rewrites for-each-over-iterator/coroutine loops (dropping the step and advancing via `next()`); for arrays and slices it returns early (`if (elem) return false;`, check_stmt.c:167) and leaves the while+step shape untouched. The same shape is produced by the range form (parser.c:2394) and the C-style form (parser.c:2343).
findings.trigger: A `for` loop over an array/slice (or a range, or the C-style header) whose body reaches `continue` at least once.

findings.title: A raw NUL byte inside a string literal is silently dropped: the parser keeps only `t->text` and codegen re-derives the length with sizeof(), so `"a\0b"` becomes "a"
findings.why: lexer.h:27-29 states that a string token keeps `len` separately "because a string literal's contents may contain a NUL byte", and lexString does pass the true byte count to lxPushAt. The AST has no place for it (`struct { const char *text; } str;`, ast.h:356), so the parser drops the length here and codegen.c:2206-2210 rebuilds it from the C string: `(slice_u8){ .data = (uint8_t *)"%s", .len = sizeof("%s") - 1 }`. Everything after the first NUL disappears from both the data and the length, with no diagnostic -- a program that says `"a\0b"` silently compiles as `"a"`.
findings.trigger: A source file containing an actual NUL byte (not the two-character escape `\0`, which is copied through and works) inside a string literal.
findings.repro:
printf 'fn main() -> i32 {
    println("a\000b")
    return 0
}
' > /tmp/t_nul.extc
/home/alphayang/extC_Compiler/build/extc /tmp/t_nul.extc | grep -n '"a'   # .data = (uint8_t *)"a", .len = sizeof("a") - 1
timeout 20 /home/alphayang/extC_Compiler/build/extc --run /tmp/t_nul.extc 2>/dev/null | od -c  # -> 'a' '
' only

coverage_notes: Read src/parser.c 2441-3649 line by line (all of it, no sampling). Functions/sections covered: tail of parseFor's for-each desugaring (2441-2467, incl. the i64(0) index, the .len condition, the element copy and forDesugar); parseWhile (2469-2484); parseCoalesce/parseExpr (2495-2512); parseOr/parseAnd/parseBitOr/parseBitXor/parseBitAnd/parseEquality/parseComparison (2515-2615); atShift/parseShift (2635-2658) and the <<,>> two-token scheme; parseTerm/parseFactor (2661-2686); tokenStartsExpr (2708-2722) and parseUnary incl. the `ext` prefix, !/-/~, *p, ref (2724-2771); parsePostfix (2779-2895: e!, e?, .field/.method with dyn payload propagation, a[i]/a[lo..hi], calls); parseArgs (2911-2927); parseFnType-in-expression helpers fnParenIsTypeList/parseFnConv (2949-2975); parseLambda (2977-3070, params, capture list, return type, literal-vs-conversion); parsePrimary (3072-3417: fn lambda/conversion, dyn, int/float/string/bool/null/new, parens, anonymous literal, array literal incl. `...`, scalar conversions, struct literals, qualified names, assoc/generic calls, literal-in-condition diagnostic); looksLikeAssoc (3440-3478); countFollowingSegs (3490-3498); parseAssoc (3526-3612); parseStructLit (3622-3649). Cross-checked and found NOT to be defects: looksLikeAssoc's `<`-scan only runs when the cursor is on `<` and terminates at TK_EOF, pk() clamps to the trailing EOF token (parser.c:46-50) so no lookahead reads out of bounds; the scanner accepts keywords inside `<>`, but any such token is then rejected by parseType/expect(`>`) in already-invalid source; atShift tests only pk(1)'s kind, which is unreachable with a string token at pk(0) except in already-invalid juxtaposition (`a "<" < b`); parseAssoc's `isCall = !targs.len && at(p,"(")` is deliberate and safe because modules.c:953 returns early whenever targs are present; the i64(0) index and the `__extc_s`/`__extc_i` names cannot collide with user names (lexer reserves `__`); nested for-each loops compile and scope correctly (tested); `break` in every for form terminates correctly (tested); an unterminated match arm does not crash or hang (tested). The raw-NUL finding is reported here because this is where the token length is discarded; the lexer side is cross-referenced in lexer.json.
